sam: Heads-up — profiler shows a regression in prefix cache hit-rate for chat-heavy traffic after the kernel change. Raw numbers below, short thread so we can triage quickly.

sam: profiler dump:
```
workload: chat-session-hippo (sim)
pre-kernel-v1: prefix_cache_hit=0.62 avg_first_token_ms=18 avg_token_ms=7
post-kernel-v2: prefix_cache_hit=0.17 avg_first_token_ms=42 avg_token_ms=9
unique_prefix_keys: pre=12.3k post=26.9k
kv-lookup-misses attributable to key-mismatch: ~68%
```

lena: Oof. Any changes to key normalization/tokenization between v1 and v2? We trimmed whitespace in a recent pass. :thinking: 

sam: Yes — kernel-v2 added a token-boundary normalization step. We switched keying from raw-prefix-string -> tokenized-prefix-length + tokenhash. In doing that we accidentally dropped chat role markers ("user", "assistant") for prefixes generated by the chat stack. So chat prefixes became different hashes from previously cached completions. RAG prompts with doc meta fields also got reordered during tokenization and that blew up cardinality.

josh: Are batches mixing chat-style prefixes and single-turn completions? If the batching heuristic coalesces different prompt shapes we might evict or mis-index keys.

maya: I traced a live kv-lookup for a sample session: for the same logical convo we saw 2.1x unique keys post-v2. The tokenization reorder was the main source. Also noticed warmup only fires a SINGLE_PROMPT warmup per model, which is fine for completion but misses convo-prefix patterns.

sam: Proposed mitigations:
- revert token-boundary-only keying; restore explicit role markers into canonical key (e.g., "role:user|text:..."), keep tokenhash as secondary
- add deterministic canonicalization for RAG doc markers (strip ephemeral IDs, stable sort metadata)
- change warmup strategy: send N representative convo prefixes for chat-enabled routes during model init
- update batching heuristic to include workload_type in batch key to avoid cross-mode coalescing for first-token warm paths

lena: Sounds reasonable. Kernel selection is also a lever — we picked v2 because of latency wins at high batch sizes. Could we gate kernel-v2 to non-chat routes until keying is fixed?

josh: Yes, we can add a routing flag: kernel_override for route kinds. Also we should capture a metric set for any canary: prefix_cache_hit_rate, avg_first_token_ms, p50/p95 token latency, unique_prefix_key_cardinality.

maya: I'll run a 24h synthetic chat trace and attach results here. Quick test locally showed hit-rate back to ~0.58 if we reintroduce role markers into the key, so mitigation likely valid.

infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: rollout/kernel-v2 -> canary (5% in iad) at 2026-03-18T02:00Z. Notifying eng-runtime. Use /deploy rollback if metrics breach.

sam: I'll open PR with a minimal patch to key composition + warmup change (POC PR #4123). Plan: land patch behind a feature flag, run canary against chat sims, then flip for broader rollout.

josh: Please add an automated regression test that compares pre/post unique_prefix_key_cardinality for a fixed seed workload. Also include a small fuzz harness for role ordering.

lena: cc @infra-bot add alert: prefix_cache_hit_rate drop >20% vs baseline for any model serving chat routes.

maya: Assigned. I'll post the sim logs in this thread when done.

sam: Thanks all. Once PR is up I'll @-mention reviewers. :rocket:
